topic_tag: a weavers' hall in a market town
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: For the next half century, one historian has argued, the hall served the district's weavers chiefly as their ______.

worlds.passage: In 1871 the hand-loom weavers of a hill district pooled their dues to buy a stone hall in the market town. Over the following decades the mill owners bought up the market, the bank, and most council seats, and turned the rules of each against home weaving. The hall's deed, held by the weavers jointly, was the one title in town they could not acquire, and inside its walls the old price agreement and the apprentice rules still held. The weavers refused every offer for it, the last in 1919. For the next half century, one historian has argued, the hall served the district's weavers chiefly as their ______.
worlds.explanation: As the owners took every other institution, the hall was the one place they could not take, and the weavers' old rules survived only inside it while the weavers refused to give it up, so it was their "stronghold." "Springboard" fails because the weavers kept to their trade and its apprentice rules rather than using the hall to leave it. "Showpiece" fails because the hall's value lay in being held against the owners, not in being displayed to anyone. "Switchboard" fails because nothing in the passage passes through the hall from one party to another.

springboard.quote: the old price agreement and the apprentice rules still held
springboard.why: the weavers were keeping their trade going inside the hall, not launching themselves out of it

showpiece.quote: the one title in town they could not acquire
showpiece.why: the hall mattered as something the owners could not take, a defensive role, not as something shown off

switchboard.why: the passage's mechanism is holding a position against takeover; no messages or orders are routed through the hall

worlds.passage: In 1871 the hand-loom weavers of a hill district pooled their dues to buy a stone hall in the market town. Its upper room held evening classes in bookkeeping, drafting, and shorthand, taught by members' children who worked in the city. The classes were always full, and the weavers' records show most who finished them leaving the looms within a few years for city offices. Membership fell every decade, and the dues of those who remained went largely to paying the teachers. For the next half century, one historian has argued, the hall served the district's weavers chiefly as their ______.
worlds.explanation: The hall trained weavers in office skills, those who trained left the looms for city work, and the membership shrank as the remaining dues paid for more classes, so the hall was a "springboard" out of the trade. "Stronghold" fails because the weavers were leaving weaving, not holding on to it. "Showpiece" fails because the hall's use was teaching its own members, not displaying anything to outsiders. "Switchboard" fails because what the hall provided was training, not the passing of messages or orders between people.

stronghold.quote: leaving the looms within a few years
stronghold.why: the hall's users were abandoning the trade, the reverse of defending a position

showpiece.quote: evening classes in bookkeeping, drafting, and shorthand
showpiece.why: the hall was used for teaching its members, not for being shown to anyone

switchboard.quote: dues of those who remained went largely to paying the teachers
switchboard.why: the hall's resources went into classes, not into routing messages or orders

worlds.passage: In 1871 the hand-loom weavers of a hill district pooled their dues to buy a stone hall in the market town. They spent ten years' dues on carved oak panels and a tall front window, and each autumn hung in it the finest length of cloth from every village. City buyers and visiting tariff officials were walked through the hall before any price or duty was discussed, and the weavers held their own meetings at an inn across the street so that nothing in the hall would look worn. For the next half century, one historian has argued, the hall served the district's weavers chiefly as their ______.
worlds.explanation: The weavers decorated the hall, filled its window with their best cloth, and walked buyers and officials through it before bargaining, while doing their own business elsewhere, so it was their "showpiece." "Stronghold" fails because the hall was opened to outsiders rather than held against them. "Springboard" fails because no one used the hall to leave the trade. "Switchboard" fails because the hall impressed visitors and did not carry the weavers' business, which happened at the inn.

stronghold.quote: visiting tariff officials were walked through the hall
stronghold.why: a place opened to outside buyers and officials for viewing is not a defended position

springboard.quote: the finest length of cloth from every village
springboard.why: the weavers were displaying their trade's best work, not leaving the trade

switchboard.quote: held their own meetings at an inn
switchboard.why: the weavers kept their own business out of the hall to keep it pristine for viewing, so the hall was not the point through which their business passed

worlds.passage: In 1871 the hand-loom weavers of a hill district pooled their dues to buy a stone hall in the market town. Merchants left orders for cloth at the hall, carters left word of yarn deliveries, and weavers in town on market day left requests for spare parts or extra hands. The caretaker sorted the slips by village, and a boy from each village carried that village's bundle home every Saturday. Weavers in the remotest valleys learned of most of their work this way. For the next half century, one historian has argued, the hall served the district's weavers chiefly as their ______.
worlds.explanation: Messages from merchants, carters, and weavers came into the hall, were sorted by village, and were carried out to the right people, with answers flowing back the same way, so the hall was their "switchboard." "Stronghold" fails because the hall was open to merchants and carters and defended nothing. "Springboard" fails because the weavers used the hall to keep working at their trade, not to leave it. "Showpiece" fails because the hall's value lay in sorting and routing slips, not in being displayed.

stronghold.quote: Merchants left orders for cloth at the hall
stronghold.why: outsiders used the hall freely, so it was not a place held against anyone

springboard.quote: learned of most of their work this way
springboard.why: the hall kept weavers supplied with work at their trade rather than launching them out of it

showpiece.why: the hall's work was routing messages, which is not display
